Aurangabad.x: Aurangabad, now known officially as Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, is a city in the Indian state of Maharashtra. It sees a lot of international tourist traffic due to its proximity to the two UNESCO World Heritage Sites, namely Ajanta and Ellora caves. Aurangabad, a dream destination of Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb, founded in 1610, is known today as one of the four important cities in Maharashtra.

sights.d: A replica of the Taj Mahal, the Bibi-ka-Maqbara is the only example of the Mughal architecture of its kind in the Deccan plateau.

Bardhaman.x: Bardhaman or Barddhaman, also known as Burdwan, is the headquarters of the namesake Purba Bardhaman district of West Bengal. It is the largest agricultural centre in the state, located in what has been traditionally called the "granary of Bengal". It is a major transport centre with rail and road connections all around.

Dooars.x: The Dooars region covers the foothills of the Himalayas in North Bengal and Assam, and an eastern extension of Nepal's Tarai region. It is home to animal species like the famous one-horned rhino and numerous other species of animals and birds. The region has an undulating span of tea gardens and rice plantation.

Pune.x: Pune, formerly Poona, is the second-largest city in the Indian state of Maharashtra. Vidisha.x: Vidisha is a historic city in Madhya Pradesh, India. Known for its ancient temples, archaeological sites, and cultural heritage, Vidisha is a must-visit destination for history enthusiasts and travellers exploring central India. Located about 60 km northeast of Bhopal, Vidisha is often overshadowed by the nearby UNESCO World Heritage Site of Sanchi, but it holds its own as a treasure trove of ancient history and architecture.
